blocks.text: The currency derivatives market in India is regulated by a hybrid model involving both RBI and SEBI.

items: RBI (Reserve Bank of India): Regulates the underlying currency market and foreign exchange policies (FEMA).
SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India): Regulates the exchanges (NSE/BSE), brokers, and the trading platform where derivatives are traded.

blocks.text: FEMA is the primary law governing forex in India. It divides transactions into two categories:

items: Current Account Transactions: Trade in goods/services (e.g., travel, imports). Freely permitted unless restricted.
Capital Account Transactions: Alter assets/liabilities outside India (e.g., buying property abroad). Restricted unless permitted.

blocks.text: Important Limit: Resident Indians and NRIs can take positions in USD-INR up to USD 100 Million without underlying exposure documentation. Above this limit, they must prove they have actual export/import exposure.
